messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: synth-canary-apac-02 triggered (5/5 failures)
incident-bot: check: synthetic/canary/apac-02 · severity: page · runbook: /runbooks/synth-canary.md
pagerduty: PagerDuty incident PD-61823 created and escalated to oncall
Ava SRE: acked on PD · I'm taking this
Carla Eng: seen, ping if you want help with reproducing or log pulls
Ava SRE: quick summary: canary probe started returning 503s ~03:20 UTC across apac-02 cluster; other regions look fine so far
Jules Support: any customer-facing errors reported? Support queue has 1 chat about slow completion in apac, not widespread yet
Ben Platform: looking at canary dashboard now — failure rate jumped from 0% to ~90% in last 2m, samples show upstream 503s from service:inference-router-apac
Ava SRE: running quick curl to synthetic endpoint to reproduce:
```
curl -v https://synth-canary-apac-02.redwood-inference.internal/ping
> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
> Server: envoy
> x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 5
```
Ava SRE: envoy is returning 503 from upstream, need to see if pods are unhealthy or cluster networking is dropping requests
Ravi Infra: checking node/host health and networking, pulling kube events for apac-02
Carla Eng: past 30m deploys? I don't see any code deploys for inference-router in apac in the last hour (checked deploy-service)
Ben Platform: there was an infra config push 00:58 UTC for CDN edge routing to apac regions (rollback candidate)
Ava SRE: thanks — Ravi can you check CDN/edge changes? Could be misrouting to cold pool causing 503s
Ravi Infra: looking at CDN logs now — I see a spike of 502/503 responses from origin around 03:18 UTC, many requests from edge-pop: ap-southeast-1b
Ravi Infra: also seeing repeated TCP resets from a small subset of nodes (10.48.23.*) in apac-02 cluster
Ava SRE: ok, let's triage: 1) snapshot pod health 2) check k8s events 3) tail envoy logs 4) consider muting noisy synthetic alert while we investigate
Carla Eng: grabbing pod list:
```
kubectl -n infra get pods -l app=inference-router -o wide --context=apac-02
inference-router-57f9b9   2/2 Running   3   12m   10.48.23.17
inference-router-62bd02   1/2 CrashLoopBackOff   5   8m   10.48.23.18
inference-router-7ab3c1   2/2 Running   0   20m   10.48.23.19
```
Ava SRE: interesting — one pod in CrashLoopBackOff, others show high restart counts; might be resource pressure or OOM from a config change
Ben Platform: checking node metrics for 10.48.23.* — CPU steady, but memory on 10.48.23.18 been pegged, oom_kill traces present
Ravi Infra: pulling dmesg from node 10.48.23.18 now
Ravi Infra: dmesg shows oom-killer invoked for envoy process around 03:16 UTC
Ava SRE: that aligns with canary failures, if envoy died requests return 503s. Any clue why memory spiked?
Carla Eng: recent envoy config tweak merged 00:55 UTC adjusted connection buffer sizes and a new filter was enabled in apac-hotpath. Could cause memory regression
Ava SRE: can we roll that filter back quickly on apac? If it's a config flag we can patch daemonset to disable
Ben Platform: preparing a conservative rollback patch for envoy filter, will apply to apac-02 only and watch
Ava SRE: also muting the synthetic to avoid page storms — will mute for 15m with note
incident-bot: Mute set: synthetic/canary/apac-02 for 15 minutes by Ava SRE · reason: active mitigation
Ava SRE: applying patch now:
```
kubectl -n infra set env ds/envoy FILTER_X_ENABLED=false --context=apac-02
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/envoy --context=apac-02
```
Ravi Infra: restart kicked, pods are coming back up
Carla Eng: tailing envoy logs for restarted pods; seeing fewer OOMs, memory stabilizing
Ava SRE: re-running curl to synth endpoint:
```
curl -v https://synth-canary-apac-02.redwood-inference.internal/ping
> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
> Server: envoy
> x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 20
```
Ava SRE: synth green at 03:29 UTC, failure rate back to 0%
Ben Platform: removing mute in 5 min after we confirm stability; will keep extra 5m retention on metrics for the moment
Jules Support: I'll post a short note in #support-status: "Transient canary failure in APAC, services recovering, no widespread customer errors detected."
Ava SRE: creating incident summary for PD-61823 and tagging it as Sev3 — root cause suspected env filter memory regression; workaround: disable filter in apac until patch lands
Carla Eng: follow-up action: schedule a canary test for the filter in staging with memory load scenarios, add guardrails to detect similar spikes
Ravi Infra: also will run a node-level OOM audit for last 24h and add alert for envoy memory delta > 200MB in apac clusters
Ben Platform: handoff note — I'm on next shift in 40m, will monitor until then, if things reflare ping me; otherwise I'll close PD-61823 after 1h stable
Ava SRE: ack, thanks everyone. Closing this thread once PD updated and support note posted. :white_check_mark:
